newsitem.title: CHINA: New tremor hits quake-plagued China region.
newsitem.headline: New tremor hits quake-plagued China region.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 5.0 on the Richter scale shook a seismically active area of China's northwestern region of Xinjiang on Saturday, but there were no reports of any casualties, a seismological official said.
The earthquake, the third to shake the area in Xinjiang's Kunlun mountains in less than a week, struck at 9.50 a.m (0150 GMT) on Saturday morning, the official said by telephone.
There were not expected to be reports of injuries or damage in the sparsely populated region, he said.
"A 5.0 (earthquake) will not cause casualties in such a mountainous area with so few people," the official said.
The tremor, which was felt in nearby towns, hit about 100-150 km (60-90 miles) from the epicentre of an earthquake measuring 7.1 on the Richter scale that shook the area on Tuesday, he said.
The Tuesday earthquake was followed by an aftershock measuring 5.1 on the scale on Friday, but there were no reports of injuries or serious damage from either tremor.
All the earthquakes occurred along the same fault line, the official said.
Chinese experts say the country is experiencing a period of increased seismological activity that is expected to last until the end of the century.
A total of 50 earthquakes measuring more than 5.0 on the Richter scale hit China in 1995, an increase of 18.5 percent from the year before, official figures show.
